newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar takes breather as mark reigns in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Dollar takes breather as mark reigns in Singapore.

text.p: The U.S. dollar continued to consolidate on Friday with an immediate downward bias against the mark as the German currency remained bid against the yen and European crosses, Singapore dealers said.
They said the mark's rise versus the yen was helping the dollar maintain a firm bias against the yen, but the U.S. unit looked heavy near 118 yen.

"I think mark/yen is going to recover more. It's already risen three big figures in the last few days," a European bank dealer said. But the cross was likely to face a temporary barrier at the 65 level.
He said the dollar's upside against the mark would be capped around the 1.8450 level for the time being, with scope for further declines towards 1.81 marks.
"Ever since we broke 1.85 convincingly, we traded back once and haven't touched anything near that level anymore," he said.
"For the time being, people have reassessed their positions and after a lot of profit-taking, it's only natural the dollar should come back down," he said.
But the dollar's fundamentals had not changed and after a period of consolidation, players were likely to realise the dollar was still a buy, he said.
